messages.author: 73fb61795976b321
messages.subject: Help with estimation of latent mean and variance.
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to get lavaan to correctly estimate the latent variable mean and variance.

According to the lavaan tutorial,  the cfa() and sem() functions fix the latent variable intercepts (which in this case correspond to the latent means) to zero. So setting std.lv=FALSE has no effect, correct?

I tried to switch to the lavaan function, but I could only get it to run using int.lv.free=FALSE which is what I do not want. The call below works.

lavaan.model.fit <- lavaan( lavaan.model.std.lv.false, 
                            data = dU2 , 
                            std.lv=FALSE,
                            parameterization="delta",
                            int.ov.free=TRUE,
                            int.lv.free=FALSE,    
                            auto.fix.first =TRUE, 
                            auto.fix.single = FALSE, # NOT_DEFAULT should not make any difference
                            auto.var=TRUE,
                            auto.cov.lv.x=FALSE,     # NOT_DEFAULT
                            auto.th=FALSE,           # NOT_DEFAULT
                            auto.delta =FALSE,       # NOT_DEFAULT
                            auto.cov.y = TRUE     
                        )

But, when I set int.lv.free=TRUE in the call above, I get the warning indicating that the information matrix could not be inverted.

1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix
My code is attached for your reference. Theta is set to a mean of 0.5 and variance of 1. But the mean is always estimated in zero. I am running out of ideas and any help would be highly appreciated.

As for background, I am trying to reproduce the results in the Kamata and Bauer results in the paper "A Note on the Relation Between Factor  Analytic and Item Response Theory
Models". I need to get the means and variance of the latent variable (Xi) to apply the formulas in the "reference Indicator" column below. When the latent variable is standardized (std.lv=TRUE), the formulas on the column "Standardized Factor" work as a charm! 


Given the following model.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Help with estimation of latent mean and variance.
parts: So setting std.lv=FALSE has no effect, correct?
Correct.  You can always free latent intercepts in the model syntax.

But, when I set int.lv.free=TRUE in the call above, I get the warning indicating that the information matrix could not be inverted.

1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
If you free latent means, you still need to identify the mean structure by fixing an intercept per factor to 0.
Theta is set to a mean of 0.5 and variance of 1. But the mean is always estimated in zero.

What "mean"?  And do you mean "fixed" rather than "estimated"? 

If you have categorical items, then intercepts are fixed to 0 to identify the latent item responses, so that information is not available to identify latent common-factor means.  Read Wu & Estabrook (2016) for a thorough discussion of these issues.  See my attached slides for a summary, along with lavaan syntax for demonstrations.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Lastly,

What about firstly?  I didn't see a question above, but if you are concerned about the warning that your model might not be identified, try identifying the common-factor mean and variance, perhaps the same way you identify the LIR intercepts and residual variances.
do I have to worry about the options below?

You can see the defaults:

lavop <- lavInspect(fit, "options")
lavop$meanstructure
lavop$int.ov.free
...
meanstructure If TRUE, intercepts/means will be added to the model both for both observed and latent variables.
This is TRUE by default with categorical data.
int.ov.free If FALSE, the intercepts of the observed variables are fixed to zero.
Default with categorical data.
int.lv.free If FALSE, the intercepts of the latent variables are fixed to zero.
Default even with continuous data.

std.lv If TRUE, the metric of each latent variable is determined by fixing their variances to 1.0. If FALSE, the metric of each latent variable is determined by fixing the factor loading of the first indicator to 1.0.
This would solve your identification issue.
